name: Life State Custody
definition: Holds the data that describes the life of the user. Organises it and serves it. All agents read the same data.
rationale: Agents keep their own part of the data. Their answers do not agree.

name: Life Data Ingestion
definition: Acquires data from external sources continuously. The user does not move data between systems.
rationale: Data that a person moves arrives late, or does not arrive.

name: Agent Coordination
definition: Sends work to agents. Lets an agent get an answer from another agent. Resolves contention. All of this occurs in a declared hierarchy.
rationale: The set of agents has no coordinator. The position of an agent must set its authority.

name: Work Management
definition: Holds work as tasks. Keeps the tasks through sessions and interruptions.
rationale: Work must continue after the conversation that made it stops.

name: Condition Detection and Initiation
definition: Evaluates declared conditions against life state. Starts contact with the user without a request.
rationale: The system cannot start work by itself without a scheduled evaluation and a channel to the user.

name: Conversation and Reach
definition: Accepts and returns interaction by speech and by text. The user can use any client.
rationale: The user speaks on a telephone and writes on a laptop. An exchange must continue on either one.

name: Authorization
definition: Stops a declared class of action until the user gives an affirmative answer.
rationale: You cannot reverse some actions. Some actions reach other people.

name: External Actuation
definition: Makes changes outside the system, such as to a calendar, a file, a message or an external system.
rationale: An agent that cannot act can only give advice.

name: Provenance
definition: Records how the system got a value, and if the system observed the value or inferred it.
rationale: You cannot tell the difference between an inference that looks like a fact and an error.

name: Agent Lifecycle Governance
definition: Defines, makes, changes, retires and keeps agent definitions under change control.
rationale: Agents are components. Their number will increase. REQ-PL-022 keeps what states an agent after the loss of the host, and a copy of a body is a property of holding that body (DEC-020), so this function keeps the definitions as well as changing them. FUN-PL-01 already states both for life state.

name: Self-Observation
definition: Reports the cost, the health and the usage of the system itself.
rationale: A limit that you find after you pass it is not a limit.

name: Behavioural Learning
definition: Derives patterns and preferences from observed data. These are more than the preferences that the user states.
rationale: A user states only some of their preferences.

name: Maintenance Work
definition: Raises the work that the platform needs to continue to operate, and sends that work to be done by an agent or by the user.
rationale: A credential stops being valid. A new source needs approval. The platform cannot continue, and no agent raised the need. The platform does not do operational work alone (DEC-015), so the work goes to an agent or to the user. Which of the two is not a property of the work: REQ-PL-012 decides whether an action needs the authorization of the user, and it decides the same way for this work as for any other.

name: Interface Description
definition: Describes the interface of the platform to the callers that use it: to an agent that the platform runs, and to a client that another person wrote.
rationale: An agent that must know what to ask of a system, how a resource is named and what a refusal means takes that account from somewhere. A copy of it in each definition drifts, which is the failure that DEC-019 states. FUN-PL-10 makes, changes and retires agents and does not state this, and a second clause in that row would be covered by REQ-PL-016 and invisible to the coverage check of MET-017. REQ-PL-011 is the same capability read from outside the platform, so it moves here from FUN-PL-06, which is speech, writing and clients.
